newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese politicians unite in drugs campaign.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese politicians unite in drugs campaign.

text.p: Portuguese politicians from across the spectrum united on Tuesday in an unprecedented publicity blitz against drug abuse, visiting schools and holding public meetings across the country.

From President Jorge Sampaio of the ruling Socialists to Communist Party leader Carlos Carvalhas, politicians and public figures took to the streets to campaign against the growing use of hard drugs by young people.

The number of registered drug addicts in Portugal has surged over the past decade to over 60,000, while the country ranks third in Europe after Spain and Italy in per capita terms in drugs-related AIDS cases.
Portugal is an important staging post for the importing of drugs such as heroin, cocaine and cannabis into Europe from Africa and South America.

"We need to create a national mobilisation against what is public enemy number one for Portugal's young and its families," Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said during a visit to a school on the outskirts of Lisbon.

Under the slogan "life is not a drug", which is a play on words as the Portuguese for drug (droga) also means a bore or a drag, the national campaign was due to end in Lisbon with a concert in a shopping centre to be attended by Guterres and Sampaio.
Newspapers carried special supplements on drug use, while schools suspended normal classes to devote time to debating the problem.
